name: Rename task
action: Open the custom project, open the task's row menu, choose Rename task, type the new name, Save — and wait until the tile renders under the new title

params.name: projectName
params.description: Custom project holding the task — its visible title

params.name: taskTitle
params.description: Current visible task title, e.g. 'Build strategies'

name: Delete task
action: Open the custom project, open the task's row menu, choose Delete task and accept the confirm dialog — then wait until the tile is gone

params.name: projectName
params.description: Custom project holding the task — its visible title

name: Rename custom project
action: Open the project row's gear menu, choose Rename custom project, type the new name, Save — and wait until the row renders under the new title

verify.note: the project LIST REBUILDS on rename (reloadProjects), so the row re-renders under the NEW name — unlike databank tabs

name: Delete custom project
action: Open the project row's gear menu, choose Delete custom project, accept the shell 'Remove project' confirm — then wait until the row is gone

params.name: projectName
params.description: Visible project title to delete — the list rebuilds on rename, so pass the CURRENT title

name: Create custom project
action: Open the New project modal, type the name, Create — and wait until the row appears in the project list. NOTE: creating with an EXISTING name silently recycles that project instead of erroring (see tests/ui/docs/NEEDS.md).

params.name: name
params.description: Name for the new custom project

name: Add task
action: Open the custom project, open the Add new task modal, click the task type, close the picker (choosing a type leaves it OPEN — proven in Tasks.add()) — then wait until the new tile renders (a server round-trip). NOTE: the APP names the task itself ('Build strategies', 'Build strategies 2', …), so pair with projects.tasks.rename when a predictable title is needed.

params.name: projectName
params.description: Custom project to add the task to — its visible title

params.name: taskType
params.description: Task type's VISIBLE label exactly as the picker shows it — 'Build strategies', 'Optimize strategies', 'Retest strategies', 'Filter strategies', 'Clear databanks', 'Go to task', … (the names taskmanager/getAvailableTasks returns); kebabbed into new-task-type-{taskType|kebab}

verify.note: strict only for the FIRST task of a type — a later same-type task is numbered ('Build strategies 2'), whose tile testid this verify cannot predict, and the first tile is already visible; the Playwright model waits on tile COUNT instead (Tasks.add()), which a flow verify cannot express
